title: A later edit against a learned rule proposes narrowing it
description:
When a person's edit undoes what a learned rule made the drafter do, the learner proposes narrowing or retiring that rule, with the edit as evidence. This is the guard against drift: learned rules are held to the same evidence that created them, and the proposal again waits for an admin.

**Acceptance criteria**
- An edit that contradicts a learned rule raises one proposal to narrow or retire it.
- Nothing is narrowed without acceptance.
- Every behaviour change ships with narrative Gherkin specs (below).

**Gherkin features needed**
- learned-contradiction.feature: an edit against a learned rule proposes narrowing; repeated contradiction strengthens the proposal instead of opening another; acceptance changes the next draft.

**Infrastructure as code touched:** None.

**Part of:** Announcements learn from a person's edits. Slice code O6 in `docs/design/always-on-agents-architecture.md` (section 12).
**Standing rules:** no fallbacks, no workarounds, no interim systems, no arbitrary caps; no text in DynamoDB; indexes over scans; no AppSync subscriptions; nothing created by hand in AWS; no real email addresses in specs or fixtures; status shown as words and marks, never colour alone.
